used_quotes: A cynic is a man who knows the price of everything and the value of nothing.
A good briefing tells you what happened. A great one tells you what people are arguing about.
A society grows great when old men plant trees in whose shade they shall never sit.
A wise man proportions his belief to the evidence.
Action is eloquence.
Ah, but a man's reach should exceed his grasp, / Or what's a heaven for?
All things are an exchange for fire, and fire for all things, as goods for gold and gold for goods.
Appearances are a glimpse of the unseen.
As soon as the land of any country has all become private property, the landlords, like all other men, love to reap where they never sowed.
Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof: and the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
Between the idea / And the reality / Between the motion / And the act / Falls the Shadow.
Beware of little expenses; a small leak will sink a great ship.
Cities have the capability of providing something for everybody, only because, and only when, they are created by everybody.
Doubt is not a pleasant condition, but certainty is absurd.
Every day is a journey, and the journey itself is home.
Every passion borders on the chaotic, but the collector's passion borders on the chaos of memories.
Facts are stubborn things; and whatever may be our wishes, our inclinations, or the dictates of our passions, they cannot alter the state of facts and evidence.
For one human being to love another: that is perhaps the most difficult of all our tasks... the work for which all other work is but preparation.
Give me a lever long enough and a fulcrum on which to place it, and I shall move the world.
Gold is money. Everything else is credit.
How did you go bankrupt?… Gradually and then suddenly.
How we spend our days is, of course, how we spend our lives.
I refute it thus.
I turn the wheel that spins; I delight to see the high come down and the low ascend.
In every chain of reasoning, the evidence of the last conclusion can be no greater than that of the weakest link of the chain, whatever may be the strength of the rest.
In the absence of the gold standard, there is no way to protect savings from confiscation through inflation.
In the fields of observation, chance favours only the prepared mind.
Insist on yourself; never imitate.
Institutions will try to preserve the problem to which they are the solution.
It is easier to build strong children than to repair broken men.
It is not the oath that makes us believe the man, but the man the oath.
It is the mark of an educated mind to be able to entertain a thought without accepting it.
It may be observed in general that the future is purchased by the present.
Man is least himself when he talks in his own person. Give him a mask, and he will tell you the truth.
Memory is the treasury and guardian of all things.
Men, it has been well said, think in herds; it will be seen that they go mad in herds, while they only recover their senses slowly, and one by one.
Nature loves to hide.
No man is an island, entire of itself; every man is a piece of the continent.
No man is good enough to govern another man, without that other's consent.
Not everything that counts can be counted, and not everything that can be counted counts.
Nothing in life is to be feared, it is only to be understood.
Peace cannot be kept by force; it can only be achieved by understanding.
Peace hath her victories, no less renown'd than war.
Price is what you pay. Value is what you get.
Reality is that which, when you stop believing in it, doesn't go away.
Safety and certainty in oil lie in variety, and variety alone.
Somewhere, something incredible is waiting to be known.
Sunlight is said to be the best of disinfectants; electric light the most efficient policeman.
The Moving Finger writes; and, having writ, / Moves on: nor all thy Piety nor Wit / Shall lure it back to cancel half a Line, / Nor all thy Tears wash out a Word of it.
The beginning is the most important part of the work.
The best way out is always through.
The condition upon which God hath given liberty to man is eternal vigilance.
The cost of a thing is the amount of what I will call life which is required to be exchanged for it, immediately or in the long run.
The first principle is that you must not fool yourself — and you are the easiest person to fool.
The future is already here — it's just not very evenly distributed.
The hand is the cutting edge of the mind.
The large print giveth, and the small print taketh away.
The map is not the territory.
The old order changeth, yielding place to new, / And God fulfils himself in many ways, / Lest one good custom should corrupt the world.
The owl of Minerva spreads its wings only with the falling of the dusk.
The quality will be remembered long after the price is forgotten.
The real voyage of discovery consists not in seeking new landscapes, but in having new eyes.
The signal is the truth. The noise is what distracts us from the truth.
The spectacle is not a collection of images; it is a social relation between people that is mediated by images.
The truth is rarely pure and never simple.
There are more things likely to frighten us than there are to crush us; we suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
There are no shortcuts to any place worth going.
There is a tide in the affairs of men, which, taken at the flood, leads on to fortune; omitted, all the voyage of their life is bound in shallows and in miseries.
Thirty spokes share the wheel's hub; it is the centre hole that makes it useful. … Therefore profit comes from what is there; usefulness from what is not there.
To see what is in front of one's nose needs a constant struggle.
To travel hopefully is a better thing than to arrive, and the true success is to labour.
Trust, but verify.
Two things fill the mind with ever new and increasing admiration and awe, the more often and steadily we reflect upon them: the starry heavens above me and the moral law within me.
Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown.
War is merely the continuation of policy by other means." — Carl von Clausewitz, *On War* (1832)
We shape our buildings; thereafter they shape us.
We shape our tools, and thereafter our tools shape us.
Well done is better than well said.
When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure.
When the facts change, I change my mind — what do you do, sir?
When we try to pick out anything by itself, we find it hitched to everything else in the Universe.
When you can measure what you are speaking about, and express it in numbers, you know something about it … but when you cannot measure it … your knowledge is of a meagre and unsatisfactory kind.
When you have to make a choice and don't make it, that is in itself a choice.
Where is the wisdom we have lost in knowledge? Where is the knowledge we have lost in information?
Whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent.
You have power over your mind — not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength.
“All of humanity’s problems stem from man’s inability to sit quietly in a room alone.”
“Though the mills of God grind slowly, yet they grind exceeding small; / Though with patience He stands waiting, with exactness grinds He all.”
“Whosoever commands the sea commands the trade; whosoever commands the trade of the world commands the riches of the world, and consequently the world itself.”

issues.quote: The cost of a thing is the amount of what I will call life which is required to be exchanged for it, immediately or in the long run.
issues.author: Henry David Thoreau, *Walden* (1854)
issues.note: Weekend-into-week briefing, 24pp; led on Anthropic's $965B confidential S-1 (1 Jun, narrowly above OpenAI's $852B March mark) \& the Hormuz 60-day MOU returned to Tehran for Trump's third edit (Brent $94.58, −17.4% m/m); Pritam Singh's requisitioned 28 Jun cadre conference with a secret-ballot trigger; the launch of "Screen Smart from the Start" with bescreensmart.gov.sg (only 37% of SG parents confident); HDB Q1 2026 RPI's first dip since 2019 (−0.1% q/q) yet a record 412 $1M flats; Microsoft Build 2026 cuts the OpenAI cord — Project Polaris replaces GPT-4 in Copilot by August, Claude Opus 4.8 \& Sonnet 4.6 land first-party in Azure AI Foundry; MiniMax M3 the first open-weight model to top SWE-Bench Pro at 59.0%; Sony A7R VI ships 4 Jun \& Sennheiser Momentum 5 ships 30 Jun with a screwdriver-replaceable battery; Home Assistant 2026.6 brings Matter onboarding over BLE proxies; Watches \& Wonders centres on Patek's 50th-anniversary Nautilus quartet (2,000-piece 5810/1G) \& the 958G pocket watch; Nolan's $250M all-IMAX-70mm *Odyssey* + Spielberg's *Disclosure Day*; Taylor's Version finale (6 Jun); *Taiwan Travelogue* wins Mandarin's first Booker International; Family Desk on the screen-smart toolkit + APA's gaming risk note; Whisper Desk on Hollywood's separation season (Biggs/Mollen, Daddario/Form confirmed); Curiosities on NASA Goddard's promise of \~100,000 Roman-discovered worlds \& a diamond-core planet; Love \& Life on Tinder's "clear-coding" \& the Wheatley/IFS dating recession; Fitness on the case against over-extending zone 2 (Schoenfeld et al. 2026); Diary led by Sanno Matsuri's even-year procession, Sumida fireworks \& the World Cup opening (11 Jun). THE LONG READ: "What's the Quote?" — Thoreau's cost-of-a-thing anchor pulls three threads (valuation theatre, negotiation as performance, industrialisation of attention) through Newton/South Sea Bubble (1720, Odlyzko on the \~£20,000 loss), Smith's diamond-water paradox (*Wealth of Nations*, 1776), the Vienna Congress \& Panmunjom armistice as "negotiation under continuous costly action," and Lippmann's *Public Opinion* (1922, "The World Outside and the Pictures in Our Heads"); callbacks to Korzybski (No. 09) \& Feynman (No. 08). Editorial theme: *the price of anything*.

issues.quote: The best way out is always through.
issues.author: Robert Frost, *A Servant to Servants* (1914)

THE LONG READ: "The Toll and the Way Around" -- chokepoints & the bypass, via the Oresund Sound Dues (1429-1857, bought out by the 1857 Copenhagen Convention), Vasco da Gama's 1498 Cape route around Venice, & Robert Fortune's 1848 theft of tea; callbacks to Thoreau (No. 10) & Korzybski (No. 09). Editorial theme: *through, or around*.

issues.quote: To travel hopefully is a better thing than to arrive, and the true success is to labour.
issues.author: Robert Louis Stevenson, *El Dorado* (1881)
issues.note: Weekend Edition, 24pp; led on the Hormuz peace "described in every capital and signed in none" (Iran's stalled messaging vs. Rubio's "talks still live") & oil's relief-to-fear whiplash (Brent ~US$95, ~-10% m/m), with Colombia's 21 Jun runoff & Ukraine's oil-infra drone war as secondaries; WP's 28 Jun secret-ballot cadres conference over Pritam Singh & the oil shock in SG tariffs (29.72c/kWh, sharper Q3 hike flagged); HDB RPI's first dip since 2019 (203.4, -0.1% q/q) beside a record 400+ million-dollar flats; the H200 cleared for China yet selling ~nothing as Beijing steers to Huawei Ascend, Anthropic's confidential ~$965B S-1 (no date) topping OpenAI's $852B, MiniMax M3 leading open weights at SWE-Bench Pro ~59%; Sony a7R VI ships (4 Jun) & Sennheiser Momentum 5 (mid-Jun) vs. Fujifilm's first cameraless June; Home Assistant 2026.6 "Pick a card" + two-way IR & Z-Wave lock PINs (legacy template syntax removed); Watches & Wonders' Nautilus-50 & Sotheby's 15 Jun "Shapes of Cartier" vs. the boutique chill; Toy Story 5 / Nolan's all-IMAX *Odyssey* & the Women's Prize (11 Jun); Family on the age-verification era (Australia under-16, US state laws, KOSA) + a "don't be alarmist" box; Whisper on Hollywood's separation season (all flagged); Curiosities on 3I/ATLAS leaving forever & SETI's Allen-Array silence ("the looking was the win") + JWST-MIRI methanol; Love & Life on relationship quality beating singlehood & the Harvard study; Fitness on VO2 max as the #1 longevity marker & muscle as "magic sauce" + a peptide-hype sceptic box; Diary led by BTS's four-night National Stadium return (first 7-member show in 7 years) & the summer matsuri. THE LONG READ: "The city that was never there" — the things that refuse to arrive (an unsigned peace, a refused chip, a passing comet, a dateless IPO) and why the hopeful travelling toward them is where the living happens, via Stevenson's *El Dorado* (1881), Ralegh's Manoa/Orinoco hunt (1595/1617), Halley's comet & Le Gentil's two failed transits of Venus (1761/1769); callbacks to Korzybski (No. 09), Thoreau (No. 10) & Frost (No. 11); the one real arrival being BTS's homecoming. Editorial theme: *travel hopefully*.

issues.quote: Well done is better than well said.
issues.author: Benjamin Franklin, *Poor Richard's Almanack* (1737)
issues.note: Weekend Edition, 24pp; led on the Hormuz 60-day MOU "described in every capital and signed in none" (Iran suspended talks 1 Jun over Israel's Lebanon push; Hezbollah reportedly accepted a US ceasefire; Trump: deal reachable "over the next week," needs "a few more points") & oil's whipsaw above US$100 then back to ~US$97 Brent (−12% m/m, 6th straight US inventory draw), with Ukraine's drone on Putin's St Petersburg forum (+ Volgograd refinery offline) & Colombia's 21 Jun runoff (de la Espriella 43.7% vs Cepeda 40.9%) as secondaries; WP's 28 Jun secret-ballot cadres conference over Pritam Singh (account→resign→ballot) & the oil shock reaching the July electricity tariff (29.72c/kWh, sharper hike flagged); the SORA-trough refinancing window (3M SORA ~1%) & June BTO (6,900 flats); the H200 cleared for China yet ~undelivered as Beijing steers to Huawei, the open-weight surge (DeepSeek V4 Pro / Qwen 3.7 Max / Kimi) & frontier-class models now running on desk hardware (DGX Spark, M5 Max, RTX Pro 6000); FUJIKINA & the expected Fujifilm X-T6 (40MP) + Leica's own sensor silicon; Home Assistant local-first (OpenThread BR, native mDNS, Matter sirens); Sotheby's "Shapes of Cartier" 15 Jun & Christie's Patek 3448G "Red Dot"; Olivia Rodrigo's 3rd album (12 Jun) & Taylor Swift's Toy Story 5 single; Family on the age-verification era (Australia under-16, KOSA) + parental-habits-beat-bans + a VPN-spike "don't be alarmist" box; Whisper's engagement/split season (all flagged); Curiosities on JWST's first mid-infrared fingerprint of 3I/ATLAS (the encore) & June's Venus–Jupiter conjunction; Love & Life on relationship quality over status (Folk & Dunn 2026); Fitness on rapamycin possibly blunting exercise gains (Stanfield et al. 2026) & banking VO₂ max early + a sceptic box; Diary led by BTS's National Stadium homecoming & the summer matsuri (even-year Sanno, Gion, Tenjin) + a teamLab art strip. THE LONG READ: "The Said and the Done" — Franklin's maxim on the gap between announcement and execution, via the Kellogg–Briand Pact (1928, war renounced by ~62 signatures with no enforcement), Prohibition / the Volstead Act (1920–33, a ban that manufactured its own evasion → age-gates & VPNs, the cleared-but-unshipped H200) & the Potemkin-village legend (1787, itself likely fabricated — a fake about fakery → vaporware), with the inversion that the week's real deeds (Ukraine's leverage, open weights actually running, the quiet homecomings) outran their words; callbacks to Stevenson (No. 12), Frost (No. 11), Thoreau (No. 10) & Korzybski (No. 09). Editorial theme: *the said and the done*.

issues.quote: In the fields of observation, chance favours only the prepared mind.
issues.author: Louis Pasteur (lecture, University of Lille, 1854)
issues.note: Weekend Edition, 24pp; led on the US–Iran nuclear framework "described in every capital, signed in none" (IAEA's Grossi signals it's close, fresh US oil-smuggling sanctions, Trump's "a few more points"; Iran's negotiator: the winner is whoever is better prepared the day after it's signed) & Brent's nervous retreat to ~US$93–95 (−6% m/m, 6th straight US inventory draw, Chinese imports a 10-yr low, an Oman terminal blast), with Colombia's 21 Jun runoff (de la Espriella 43.7% vs Cepeda 40.9%) & Ukraine's St Petersburg oil-terminal drone strike as secondaries; SG's S$500 CDC vouchers pulled forward to June on the oil shock (Siow: no blunt across-the-board fuel-duty cut), Q1 GDP revised up to 6% on AI demand, April CPI 1.8%; the SORA-trough refinancing window (3M SORA ~1.08%, flagged closing toward ~1.39% by year-end) & HDB RPI −0.1% Q1 (first dip in ~7 yrs); the H200 licensed for China yet ~undelivered as Beijing steers to Huawei, CFR/Setser noting Huawei's own roadmap trails (no true H200-class part before the Ascend 960, late 2027) & a US AI-power-bill angle, the open-weight reshuffle (GLM-5.1 strongest all-rounder / Kimi K2.6 leads GPQA / DeepSeek V4-Pro long-context) with MiniMax M3 demoted; Oura Ring 5 ships (4 Jun, US$399, blood-pressure "Health Radar") & Kuo's cut-to-two Apple glasses roadmap (Vision Air scrapped) vs Google's audio-first Android XR glasses; Matter 1.5 cameras finally on shelves (CSA "Unify" 16–18 Jun, SmartThings first) & Ubiquiti's UniFi OS 5.1.15 Blueprint engine; Japan "still cheap, quietly cooling" (record 42.7m in 2025, ~−3% in 2026, overtourism management) & the watch-auction barometer (Christie's 10 Jun / Sotheby's "Shapes of Cartier" 15 Jun — results, not previews); the Women's Prize (11 Jun, Choi's *Flashlight*) & a quiet-arrivals / loud-anticipation culture slate (Toy Story 5, Nolan's *Odyssey*, Olivia Rodrigo demoted); Family on the evidence toolkit (Nagata/ABCD; monitoring & modelling over reward/punishment; tween 5h33m/day) + the globalising age-gate (Australia's ~4.7m closed child accounts, live AI-chatbot codes) + a "don't be alarmist" box; Whisper's engagement/split season (all flagged); Curiosities on JWST's dawn rock-clouds on WASP-94A b & the lemon-shaped pulsar planet (the prepared instrument; 3I/ATLAS now closed out); Love & Life on company-beats-solitude (Folk & Dunn 2026) & the Harvard study — social capital as a banked reserve; Fitness on banking fast-twitch power (HL-VIRT, *Experimental Gerontology* 2026) + creatine 3–5g & a longevity-discourse sceptic box; Diary led by the even-year summer matsuri (Sanno 7–17 Jun, Gion, Tenjin, Sumida fireworks) + an SG concert/art slate (BTS demoted to an undated callback). THE LONG READ: "Dig the Well Before the Thirst" — reserves laid down before the moment that demands them, via Joseph's seven-year grain store (Genesis 41), Rome's *cura annonae* & the *horrea* granaries, the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve (EPCA 1975, after the 1973–74 embargo) & Pasteur's prepared mind (the 1879 chicken-cholera serendipity → attenuated vaccine); callbacks to Frost (No. 11), Stevenson (No. 12) & Franklin (No. 13). Editorial theme: *the prepared mind / reserves before the need*.

issues.quote: Ah, but a man's reach should exceed his grasp, / Or what's a heaven for?
issues.author: Robert Browning, *Andrea del Sarto* (1855)
issues.note: **The Weekend Edition** — first Sunday lifestyle-mode issue; continuity-correct vs No. 14. 24pp geared lifestyle: cover & teasers led from Curiosities / Good Life / Kit, hard-news desks run lean. THE WORLD (2pp, TWO viewpoint panels): the Hormuz framework still "described in every capital, signed in none" — stalled over Lebanon, US escort suspended, Polymarket signing odds ~72%→~6%, Brent ~$93 — plus a reflective "slow news of a summer Sunday" digest (Colombia 21 Jun run-off; Ukraine St Petersburg/Volgograd strikes). SINGAPORE: the $500 CDC vouchers pulled forward to June (~S$1bn drawer plan, Siow) read as a household relief calendar; Q1 GDP 6%, Apr CPI 1.8%. PROPERTY: the 3M-SORA trough (~1.08%→~1.39% year-end) as a weekend refinancing job; HDB RPI −0.1% Q1. TECH: WWDC eve (8 Jun; Gemini-Siri, "27" betas, rumoured HomePad, Cook's likely-last keynote → Ternus Sept) + the home lab as a weekend project (open-weight field unchanged → "still on the shelf"; H200 one-line delta). KIT: Sony Xperia 1 VIII (NEW — jack/microSD/shutter, 48MP×3, ~S$1,989) + a "still on the shelf" strip (Oura 5 / a7R VI / Momentum 5 / smart-glasses; screwdriver-battery detail retired). CONNECTED HOME: a lifestyle "house that knows it's Sunday" feature (slow-morning scene, circadian lighting, local-first HA) — Matter 1.5 cameras CORRECTLY demoted to a one-line callback (No. 14), not re-led. GOOD LIFE: travel (Japan on a soft yen) + watch CULTURE (>40% of Sotheby's buyers under 40; cooling top-end as connoisseurship) — the NY watch week demoted to a one-line "read the results, not the previews." SCREEN & SOUND: a weekend "what to stream" (The Bear, House of the Dragon, the Lopez/Goldstein Netflix rom-com) + Rodrigo ADVANCED via a NEW angle (her Robert Smith duet revealed at Primavera Sound) + a one-line Women's Prize calendar note. FAMILY (2pp): a warm "screen-free Sunday" (SG June holidays; sleep/play/curiosity over controls; age-gates demoted to a one-liner) + a "don't be alarmist" evidence page. WHISPER: the Swift–Kelce summer-wedding rumour + engagement/split round-up (all flagged). CURIOSITIES: the Venus–Jupiter conjunction (8–9 Jun, ~1.6°, closest until 2028) as a free weekend assignment + the JWST cosmic-web map (5 Jun). LOVE & LIFE: anticipation/savoring (the pre-event peak). FITNESS: the exercise + rapamycin/lamivudine trial & a creatine RCT (Salem et al.) as longevity-lifestyle + the VO₂max-as-proxy sceptic. issues.note: **The Weekday Briefing** (standard 24pp news edition — no Travel Desk, Macro Desk standing). Issue spine: *the lag / the delayed reckoning — every cause keeps its consequence waiting; the bill, the harvest and the reading all arrive late*. Theme tag: *the bill comes due late*. THE WORLD (2pp, 4 viewpoint panels Washington/Tehran/Vienna-IAEA/Doha-Gulf): LEAD “one signature, two clocks” — the Iran 60-day deal roadmap (Doha talks resumed 1 Jul, Vance “going well,” Bürgenstock format) reading fast on paper but slow on the water: Hormuz ~35 vessels/day (⅓ of the ~110 pre-war), ~80 uncleared mines, GPS spoofing easing, the IRGC still warning, a container ship aground; ~441kg 60%-HEU last verified ~Jun 2025; Brent low-$70s, the war premium gone. p4 SECONDARY = FIFA World Cup R16 (today 6 Jul: Portugal–Spain Arlington, USMNT–Belgium Seattle; final 19 Jul MetLife) as America’s 250th “other party” (Infantino) + in-brief (Lebanon truce fraying, Ukraine refinery strikes, Colombia runoff, DXY ~101 softening, ~11,000 stranded seafarers). SINGAPORE: LEAD “the war reaches your meter” — the 1 Jul electricity tariff **+17.0%** (regulated 31.91¢/kWh before GST, 34.78¢ with; 4-room HDB +$17.14/mo) as the delayed bill — set from the 1 Apr–15 Jun gas-price window (the war weeks), 95% of power from imported gas, relief not until Q4 / possibly Q1 2027; U-Save up to $190 in July (>1M households) BUT multi-property owners INELIGIBLE (the reader eats the full increase); cross-ref World/Macro/Connected Home. Secondaries: STI record 5,244.29 (3 Jul, +30.8% YoY) vs soft SGD ~1.292; MTI 2.0–4.0% growth (Q1 6.0%); 1 Jul CPF/retirement changes one-line. PROPERTY: LEAD “a second city, tendered” (SUPPLY not rates) — the **Jurong Lake District white-site GLS** at Town Hall Link (3.72ha, tender launched 3 Jul, SG’s second CBD, a long-fuse supply bet with TOP years out). Secondaries: June BTO 22,312 applications (5 towns); the Greater Sentosa / Pulau Brani master plan (new tram); 2026 Confirmed List ~9,300 units; developer sales 447 May; CCR/landed “flight to the top” (No. 35 callback); SORA ~1% one-line. TECHNOLOGY (2pp): p7 Silicon & Sovereignty LEAD “the memory cycle goes public” — **SK hynix’s ~US$29.4bn Nasdaq ADR debut (~10 Jul)** — the ACTUAL listing = the new peg vs the No. 34/35 filing; a top-5 US listing ever; ~70% of 2026 memory chips → AI datacentres; the HBM oligopoly (SK hynix ~57–62% / Micron / Samsung); the Nvidia–SK hynix co-design pact (6 Jun); VWRA “already owns the cycle”; the OpenAI-stake + H200/China deltas one-line. p8 The Home Lab “the listing lands on your motherboard” — the RAMpocalypse (consumer RAM ~+100%, 32GB DDR5 >$370, Crucial retail retired) as the retail end of datacentre orders; the hedge = run small (Qwen 3.6-35B-A3B single-GPU pick, Gemma 4 12B/16GB, DeepSeek V4-Flash), buy RAM inside the box (Strix Halo unified memory), shift DRAM→VRAM; Ollama MLX + LM Studio KV-cache; “own the weights, rent the watts.” THE KIT: LEAD “the battery you can change” — the **Sennheiser Momentum 5 Wireless** now reviewed (What Hi-Fi 5-star, ~57h ANC, Dolby Atmos head-tracking, 42mm drivers) with a **user-replaceable battery** (nudged by EU serviceable-battery rules) as anti-obsolescence / repairability-as-deferred-value (the No. 31 “still on the shelf” → now reviewed = new peg); sceptic (replaceable ≠ effortless; glued rivals sound great); secondary = **Xreal R1 AR glasses shipping July** (~US$850, screen-tearing caveat, the sci-fi-shelf fit); Sony XM6 “ColleXion” / Garmin FR 70·170 (closed) “still on the shelf.” CONNECTED HOME (delta): “the light switch and the tariff” — ties the +17% tariff to local energy control (HA Energy dashboard, local Lutron→HA control of aircon/lights, local-first as cost-control AND a hedge vs vendor “sudden death”); HA 2026.7 (1 Jul, No. 35 lead) one-line continuity; Matter 1.6 delta; sceptic = the setpoint beats the dashboard. THE GOOD LIFE: OBJECT = the **Astell&Kern SP4000T** vacuum-tube portable DAP (quad Raytheon JAN6418 MIL-Spec tubes, Triple Tube Mode 54 voicings, >US$4,290) — the literal lag of a valve warming up as the whole spine; own-it/heirloom durability (ties the wired renaissance No. 31 + store-of-value No. 34); ESCAPE = the soft-yen ~¥160 window one-line (cross-ref Macro/Diary); tube-DAP sceptic (euphonic colour, not fidelity). SCREEN & SOUND: LEAD (music, fresh) “the summer of the sequel” — **Madonna’s *Confessions II*** (out 3 Jul, 15th album, an explicit sequel to 2005’s *Confessions on a Dance Floor*, Stuart Price reunion, lead single “Bring Your Love” ft. Sabrina Carpenter) anchoring a reinvention-July (Ariana *Petal* 31 Jul, Charli xcx *Music, Fashion, Film* 24 Jul, Steve Lacy *Oh Yeah?* 17 Jul, Tyla *A\*POP* 24 Jul, the Rolling Stones *Foreign Tongues* with a final Charlie Watts appearance) — the 21-year return as the month’s shape; the Strokes’ *Reality Awaits* now dated 24 Jul (recurring delay thread) one-line; Olivia Rodrigo SATURATED one-line. FILM (secondary, DEMOTED per the 3-consecutive-lead rule) = Nolan’s *The Odyssey* (17 Jul, IMAX 70mm, No. 35 advance-as-secondary; demand outpacing *Oppenheimer*) + *Spider-Man: Brand New Day* (31 Jul); *Toy Story 5* the lone 2026 $1bn film. THE FAMILY DESK (2pp): LEAD “the lever hiding in plain sight” — **tween sleep** (a 2026 *Clocks & Sleep* systematic review, ages 6–12: shorter/fragmented sleep → attention, memory, academics, emotional/social function; ~9–11h at age 11) with the **World Cup’s late-night matches** as a live “social jet-lag” test (cross-ref The World; hold the wake-time anchor; a few big nights fine, chronic erosion not); NOT screen-time (saturated); a “don’t be alarmist” page (one 3am quarter-final is a memory, not a wound; persistent short sleep + mood/learning change = a paediatrician); advances the desk into a NEW domain (sleep); general guidance, not medical advice. THE MACRO DESK (four instruments): “long and variable lags” (Friedman) — the regime is **rotation, not retreat** (advancing No. 35): soft June jobs (~57k vs ~110k exp, unemployment DOWN 4.2%) + the 1-yr inflation swap collapsing (~3.5%→~2.1%) fade the July-hike scare (odds ~18%); new chair **Warsh held 3.50–3.75%** at Sintra (“inflation risks have come down,” “a good family fight” at the July FOMC); a softer dollar (DXY ~101) lifting gold (~$4,170) and BTC (~$61k, after its worst-ever spot-ETF month); FRESH WRINKLE = the **Japan long-end JGB selloff** (10Y ~2.77% near a multi-decade high, 30Y >4%) as the global-bonds story + cross-ref Good Life’s soft yen. Levels to Thu 2 Jul (US shut Fri 3 Jul): VWRA ~$190, S&P ~7,500, STI 5,244, US 10Y 4.49%, USD/JPY ~¥160, USD/SGD 1.292, Brent ~$71, gold ~$4,170, BTC ~$61k; next big print = June CPI ~mid-July (awaited); the Section 122 10% tariff expires 24 Jul; regime = higher-for-longer softening / rotation / risk-on-broad / dollar-soft; standing close “what it means for VWRA, global bonds, gold & BTC”; education not advice, no fabricated prints, gold/BTC read for sensitivity only, BTC volatility flagged. CURIOSITIES: LEAD “the ten-year movie begins” — the **Vera C. Rubin Observatory’s LSST has begun** (Universe Today 30 Jun; a decade-long survey of the southern sky every few nights, catching anything that changes brightness/position, built to find the next 3I/ATLAS early — No. 35 comet tie); old light = the ultimate lag (seeing is always seeing-late; the survey reads a rate of change, not a moment). Secondaries: TESS’s first gravitational-microlensing exoplanet (a Jupiter-like world, 3 Jul); a University of Bonn dark-matter-challenge study (flagged CONTESTED, 3 Jul); NASA/Chandra’s 250th red-white-blue images (4 Jul grace note); 3I/ATLAS one-line (No. 35 closed). LOVE & LIFE: “the two kinds of alone” — self-determined vs non-self-determined solitude (attachment research via PsyPost: anxious/avoidant → “non-self-determined solitude” → intense loneliness); solitude-with-agency restorative, solitude-without corrosive, the loneliness a slow tax posted on a lag; advances (not repeats) No. 35’s friendship recession through the lever of AGENCY; nudge-not-cure caveat (correlational; structural aloneness a real exception). FITNESS (“The Long Game”): “the slowest lag of all” — the 2026 longevity-science roundup foregrounding (a) the **higher-protein target** (RDA 0.8g/kg a floor; the active-40s+ consensus ~1.2–1.6g/kg — established sports-nutrition; muscle as the account you fund years ahead) and (b) the **Becca Levy / Yale positive-aging-mindset** finding (*Geriatrics* 2026: positive attitudes about ageing → later-life cognitive/physical gains, ~4,000 adults); the settled anchor = combine strength + aerobic (~45% lower mortality, No. 32/34); observational-caveat sceptic (attitude a contributor not a controller; protein a range not a prescription); distinct from strength sweet-spot (No. 28/32), VO₂max (No. 34), Zone-2 (No. 35); general guidance, not medical advice. THE DIARY (2pp): SG — NDP 2026/SG61 (★ 9 Aug, first indoor 300-drone show, NE shows 11 & 18 Jul, previews 25 Jul & 1 Aug), EXO (★ 24–26 Jul), Into the Ocean/OceanX @ ArtScience (to 1 Nov), Flesh & Bones (to 16 Aug), NLB Sci-Fi Pop-up Library @ Parkway Parade (reader-fit), Minecraft Experience @ Mandai (to 13 Sep), Singapore Garden Festival, Sentosa GrillFest, Post Malone (22 Aug), Honne (4–6 Aug), BIGBANG (17 Oct, SG on-sale STILL pending) one-line. Japan/region — Gion Matsuri (★ 17 & 24 Jul), Sumida Fireworks (★ 25 Jul), Tenjin (24–25 Jul), Fuji Rock (24–26 Jul), Aomori Nebuta / Akita Kantō (2–7 Aug), Naadam (11–13 Jul) + planning-notes boxes. THE TABLE (rotated, fresh, honesty rule): **FreakyNoods** (Chinatown, soft-launched 1 Jul, Japanese-inspired pasta by FreakyCones, “Duck Buddy” $16.90, Eatbook-warm but “early days” — LEAD/value) + **Yi Man Fen “Sugar Rush”** (313 Somerset, China dessert-chain SG debut, ~$5.80 bowls, viral, “too new to call”, not halal) + **Madeleine’s Portuguese Egg Tarts** (Aperia, a 26-yr institution’s comeback = the culinary lag, not halal) + **Cookboys by Han’s** (I12 Katong, British-Hainanese heritage, ~$14–24, family/value); “now reviewed” = the **Tiffany Blue Box Cafe** (No. 35 “too new” → opens mid-Jul, verdict still out) one-line. **Hikiniku to Come correctly NOT relisted — the RETIRED flag (No. 28) fired again.** PHOTO EDITION heroes (4, all verified from their Commons file pages, honestly labelled): Marina Bay at dusk — File:Singapore Marina Bay Dusk 2018-02-27.jpg, CC BY-SA 4.0, Benh Lieu Song (Featured, Singapore); chips on a six-inch wafer — File:Chips on 6-Inch-Wafer 01.jpg, CC BY-SA 3.0, Kuebi / Armin Kübelbeck (representative, Technology); over-ear headphones — File:Headphones 1.jpg, CC BY-SA 2.5 (representative, NOT the reviewed Momentum 5, The Kit); the Milky Way — File:ESO - Milky Way.jpg, CC BY 4.0, ESO (Featured, Curiosities). The cover “signal arrives late” wavefront hero, the Macro four-instrument tables, the HBM memory-share bars, and the supply-fuse / sleep-debt / two-directional-fuse / “reading the rate of change” figures kept as original SVG (no forced photo). THE LONG READ (3pp): **“The Long Fuse”** — the lag as the grammar of consequence, running two ways (blast vs bloom), via **Ole Rømer’s 1676** finite-speed-of-light measurement from Io (seeing is always seeing-late; ties Rubin), **Milton Friedman’s “long and variable lags”** (ties the Macro/tariff), the **July 1914 “long fuse”** from Sarajevo to war (Lafore, *The Long Fuse*, 1965; the catastrophe-lag; brief, non-graphic; ties Iran’s 60-day clock) vs the positive harvest-lag — the planted oak (“plant trees whose shade you’ll never sit in,” Greek proverb; the New College Oxford oak-beam story flagged as embellished) and compound interest / **Bogle’s 1976** index fund (the reader’s VWRA); the discipline = read which fuse you hold (act early against the blast; keep feeding the slow good thing on the days nothing happens); the mills grind slowly but exceeding small = slow AND exact. Callbacks: Hemingway “gradually, then suddenly” (No. 34), Bashō (No. 35). Editorial theme: *the lag / the delayed reckoning*.

issues.note: **The Weekday Briefing** (standard 24pp news edition — no Travel Desk; Macro Desk standing). Issue spine: *endings, declared vs built — a peace proclaimed over vs a loop finished on schedule; the announced ending is the one to distrust, the earned one the one to trust*. Theme tag: *an ending is built, not declared*. THE WORLD (2pp, 4 viewpoint panels Washington/Tehran/Beijing/Doha-Gulf): LEAD "the sixty-day peace lasted twenty" — the US–Iran ceasefire (signed 17–18 Jun) COLLAPSED in ~48h: Iran hit 3 tankers near Hormuz (Qatari LNG + Saudi crude carrier, 7 Jul), US CENTCOM struck 80+ targets incl. Kharg Island overnight 7–8 Jul + revoked the crude waiver/reimposed sanctions; Trump at the NATO Ankara summit called the deal "over," threatened to reinstate the blockade and to "take over Kharg Island," then softened ("I don't think it's going to start again"); Brent +5.2% to $78.02 (war premium re-priced in a day); strikes landed mid-funeral (Khamenei's 7-day rites 3–9 Jul, burial Mashhad 9 Jul; successor son Mojtaba wounded/never appeared — "a leader its public has neither seen nor heard"). p4 SECONDARY = World Cup R16 done (Norway 2–1 Brazil, Haaland brace, Brazil's earliest exit since 1990; Belgium 4–1 USA; Spain 1–0 Portugal; QFs 9–11 Jul, final 19 Jul MetLife) + in-brief (NATO Ankara: Trump calls Spain a "terrible partner," Hegseth's 6-mo Europe force-posture review; IOC provisionally restores Russia's Olympic committee for LA2028; Le Pen conviction upheld but eligible for 2027 w/ ankle tag; Omsk refinery hit ~3,000km — deepest strike of the war; Lebanon strikes; Colombia runoff still contested). SINGAPORE: LEAD "the loop closes on Sunday" — Circle Line Stage 6 opens 12 Jul (Keppel/Cantonment/Prince Edward Rd; 39km/33-station loop closed after ~17 yrs; 4 Jul free-ride preview) set against a RECORD COE tender (8 Jul: Cat A S$129,000, Cat B S$130,889, Cat C S$95,000, all-category record) — the state finishes a loop making the car less necessary the week the car hits its priciest ever; STI kept climbing (5,256 Mon 6 Jul → ~5,379 Wed 8 Jul provisional, intraday >5,400); Parliament 7 Jul rail-reliability/Rail Academy; NODX June (~17 Jul) + tariff (No. 36) one-line. PROPERTY (SUPPLY/launches, NOT rates): LEAD "Turf City returns at three thousand a foot" — **Dunearn House** (Frasers/CSC/Sekisui, 380 units, first private condo of the Bukit Timah Turf City transformation, first launch in the Swiss Club orbit in ~33 yrs; preview 10 Jul, books 25 Jul; 2BR fr S$1.475M/~$2,799 psf, 3BR fr S$2.597M/$2,978 psf) vs **Lentor Gardens Residences** (Kingsford, 502 units, preview 4 Jul avg $2,350 psf, books 18 Jul, land $920 psf ppr) as the premium-on-promise control experiment; 188 million-$ HDB resales in June (monthly record, 8.8% of deals, resale prices flat); MinLaw en-bloc-threshold review (no timeline); Bayshore Drive GLS closes 15 Jul; SORA one-line. (Continuity note: Vela Bay already LAUNCHED 11 Apr 2026 — 371/515 sold day-one at avg $2,886 psf — NOT an upcoming launch; No. 34/36's "flagged" framing corrected.) TECHNOLOGY (2pp): p7 Silicon & Sovereignty LEAD "a nineteen-fold profit, and it wasn't enough" — **Samsung Q2 prelim op profit ₩89.4tn (~$58.4bn), ~19× YoY, beat — stock −6.9%**, torching chips (SOX −5.7% 4-wk low, Intel −9/AMD −8/Micron −5; memory in a bear market); same day **DeepSeek building its own inference chip** (Reuters, to route around Nvidia AND Huawei; V4 due mid-Jul w/ peak/off-peak pricing) + **SK hynix's ~$28bn Nasdaq ADR bookbuild closed a day early, oversubscribed; SKHY trades Fri 10 Jul** (largest-ever US listing by a foreign firm, would beat Alibaba; Seoul shares −17% MTD — "cycle or belief"); GPT-5.6 (Luna/Terra/Sol) public 9 Jul after the EO-14409 pre-release govt review ("ships with a regulatory green light"); Apple's >$30bn Broadcom US-chip deal (15bn chips, Fort Collins) + CXMT-DRAM-for-China testing = bifurcation. p8 The Home Lab "even the cloud has a rush hour now" — DeepSeek's peak/off-peak API pricing (inference as a load-curve utility); Ukraine to procure AI "operated without provider control" + the EU cyber-AI action plan (7 Jul) = the own-your-weights case made by everyone but owners; RAMpocalypse worse (32GB DDR5 ~$529, shortage to late 2027); HF transformers v5.13 unified exporter + Nvidia GR00T 1.7 in LeRobot; a (unverified-at-press) critical Gitea auth-bypass CVE — patch anyway. THE KIT: LEAD "the $99 earbuds that remember what you heard" — **Nothing Ear (3a)** (US$99, 45dB ANC, LDAC, IP54, 42h w/case; reviewed 7–8 Jul, "still Nothing's value king," embarrasses the $179 Ear 3) whose 32MB onboard flash enables **Audio Snapshot** (pinch = save last 60s) + call recording — a novel feature carrying a one-party-recording-etiquette sceptic (general guidance, not legal advice); secondaries = **Samsung Unpacked dated 22 Jul London** ("A New Shape Unfolds," specs = rumour) + **GoPro Mission 1 Pro** review wave ($699, best action-cam video, 8K/60, Engadget 8.7); Xreal R1 / Sony XM6 ColleXion / Oura vs Whoop "still on the shelf." CONNECTED HOME: "the house that knows you're there — without watching" — the mmWave presence-sensor arms race (**SwitchBot** ships a battery mmWave presence sensor days after **Aqara** announced its own; SwitchBot AI hub vs Echo Hub) as the input that makes HA 2026.7 room-intent automations (No. 35) finally correct — radar knows someone is present without a lens (privacy-budget bargain vs the recording earbuds/wearable backlash); pipeline = Aqara Camera Hub G350 + W200 thermostat-controller; "buy the certified device, not the announcement" (No. 31); Matter 1.6 announced≠adopted one-line. THE GOOD LIFE: OBJECT/market = "the gavel came back first" — **Phillips' spring 2026 season up ~60% to US$507M, 90% sell-through by lot** (the collector market re-heated after 2 cooling years; ties the store-of-value No. 34 thread; Heritage "Contemporary Classics" 20 Jul the mid-market test) + **Seiko Presage Cocktail Time refresh** (new HCB "double shot" models, Fratello 7 Jul — specs/pricing HELD pending) + a Studio Underd0g gen-2 grace note; ESCAPE = the soft-yen (~¥162) window (cross-ref Macro/Diary). SCREEN & SOUND: LEAD "the Emmys reward the long shift" — 2026 Emmy noms landed Wed 8 Jul (one batch; ceremony 14 Sep NBC, host Mariska Hargitay): **The Pitt 25 noms (most), Hacks 24 (comedy record), Beef tops limited; Vince Gilligan's *Pluribus* breaks into Best Drama** (genre-TV's strongest showing in years; snubs = Euphoria, Industry, The Bear's White & Moss-Bachrach); **Madonna *Confessions II*** holding (No. 36) — "best in 20 years," 13.07M day-one Spotify, UK midweek #1, Billboard 200 print this weekend (the five-decades superlative HELD); box office = softest July 4th in years (*Minions & Monsters* $61M/5-day franchise-worst; *Toy Story 5* $31M wk3; ~$121M frame) with Disney's live-action *Moana* (~$85M) opening 11 Jul, a week before *The Odyssey* (17 Jul, No. 35, now secondary); Strokes first-week chart still open (No. 28); Supergirl closes on a 77% 2nd-wk drop. THE FAMILY DESK (2pp): LEAD "who really ends a childhood sport" — Aspen Institute **Project Play** national survey (~4,000 youth 10–17, w/ Utah State & Louisiana Tech, spring 2026): girls who quit sport far likelier than boys to cite a parent who **compared them (25% vs 9%)**, pressured (24 vs 16) or argued with refs (13 vs 6); avg quit age ~13; the sideline as the rare strong/fast/free lever ("I love watching you play"); self-report/spring-2026-date caveats flagged; "don't be alarmist" p14 (incidents vs weather; most quits are structural — cost/time; a quit ≠ failure; alarm only if she stops ALL movement + withdraws); also-on-desk = UCD social-media-agency study (7 Jul, "more say not less screen"; screen-time SATURATED) + the first-daughter effect (POQ); general guidance, not medical advice. THE MACRO DESK (four instruments): "the week the market un-priced the peace" — one causal chain: Mon record Dow (53,056) → Tue chip rout (Samsung, p7, SOX −5.7%) → Wed Iran shock (Brent +5.2% $78.02) + June FOMC minutes ("a few" argued for a June hike, committee split, dot-plot-less regime) → 2Y 4.19% / 10Y 4.57%, Sep-hike odds ~58→~69%, Dow −586; VWRA's records were financed by cheap oil (clawed back); global bonds worse at both ends (10Y JGB 2.825% Mon, highest since 1996) = equities-down/bonds-down week; **gold FELL ~1% on a day of US strikes on Iran** (real-yields chain beat haven demand — the week's most instructive tell); BTC rejected at $64k, <$63k; docket = June CPI 14 Jul, SKHY Fri, Section-122 sunset 24 Jul (not relief); regime = higher-for-longer re-armed / oil re-premiumed / rotation under review / dollar steady; standing close "what it means for VWRA, global bonds, gold & BTC"; education not advice, no fabricated prints, gold/BTC read for sensitivity only. CURIOSITIES: LEAD "thirty-one lamps from the dawn" — **Euclid confirms 31 ancient quasars** (z 6.6–7.8, two the most ancient ever, first ~670 Myr; Yang et al., *A&A*, 6 Jul; a dark-energy survey as the best ancient-lamp hunter — rhymes with Vera Rubin No. 36; sharpens the early-SMBH-growth puzzle) + **Hayabusa2's Torifune flyby** (JAXA, 7 Jul, ~800m, a contact binary); in-brief = fossil-tooth-socket bee nurseries (*Royal Society Open Science*) + GWTC-5 (~390 GW detections; No. 23/25); 3I/ATLAS closed. LOVE & LIFE: "when she earns more, the old explanation fails" — a *Journal of Marriage and Family* study (via PsyPost 8 Jul) replicates the higher-earning-woman break-up pattern but finds the **traditional-gender-norms explanation doesn't hold** — the risk is the *unrenegotiated household*, not her income (re-mark the positions, don't blame the old marks); companions = a 3-type romantic-deception taxonomy (JSPR) + couples' "contagious forgetting"; observational caveats; not counselling advice. FITNESS: "the brake on ageing muscle — and the pedal that releases it" — **Duke-NUS / *Autophagy*: with age DEAF1 rises → mTORC1 overdrive → autophagy suppressed → muscle repair stalls; exercise activates FOXO which lowers DEAF1** (the molecular "use it or lose it"; mouse/cell model — NOT a prescription; sobering nuance = in very old muscle exercise alone may not fully restore repair → the argument for starting at 45 not 60); UCLA NDRG1 (3 Jul) complements; the settled prescription (strength+cardio ~45% mortality, 90–120min sweet spot, Nos. 28/32/34) is UNCHANGED; "no DEAF1 pill" sceptic; general guidance, not medical advice. THE DIARY (2pp): SG — NDP 2026/SG61 (★ 9 Aug, first indoor 300-drone show, NE shows 11 & 18 Jul), **F1 Exhibition Asian debut** (★ 23 Jul–18 Oct Gardens by the Bay, tickets on sale S$29–49), Creators Super Fest (11–12 Jul), Legally Blonde musical (29 Jul), the Weeknd (2–3 Oct), Post Malone (22 Aug), 5SOS (10–11 Nov), BTS ARIRANG (★ 17/19/20/22 Dec) + a stadium-Q4 booking note; Japan — **teamLab Borderless new exhibition** (★ 8 Jul–8 Oct "On the Asymmetry of the Universe"), Gion Matsuri (★ 17 & 24 Jul), Sumida Fireworks (25 Jul), Fuji Rock (24–26 Jul), Aki Basho sumo (13–27 Sep, tickets on-sale 8 Aug), BIGBANG HK (13–15 Nov) + planning notes. **STANDING CHASE: BIGBANG SG (17 Oct) on-sale STILL unannounced** (5th issue chasing; "Coming Soon" via b.stage). THE TABLE (rotated, fresh, honesty rule): **Mimmo Bakery Café** (Asia Square CBD; HK Quarry Bay import, pistachio bolo bao/HK egg tart; the batch's VERIFIED HIT — SETHLUI/DFD/Eatbook unanimous, LEAD) + **Casa Mori** (Dempsey; Willin Low × José Alonso Spanish-mod-Sin, one warm review in, pedigree bet) + **Hi Stranger** (Neil Rd; shape-shifting "chapters" cocktail bar, too new to call) + **Rolls** (Club St temaki bar, details held); **Blue Box Café** status-check (No. 36 lead, STILL not open — "mid-July," too new to call, honoured); Cookhouse by Koufu (Changi T2 24/7 airside) note. Not relisted: FreakyNoods/Yi Man Fen/Madeleine's/Cookboys (No. 36); Hikiniku to Come stays RETIRED (No. 28); Bouillon Gavroche flagged as stale-recirculating. PHOTO EDITION heroes (4, all verified/representative from their Commons file pages, honestly labelled): Marina Bay at dusk — File:Singapore Marina Bay Dusk 2018-02-27.jpg, CC BY-SA 4.0, Benh Lieu Song (representative, Singapore); chips on a wafer — File:Chips on 6-Inch-Wafer 01.jpg, CC BY-SA 3.0, Kuebi/Armin Kübelbeck (representative, Technology); personal audio — File:Headphones 1.jpg, CC BY-SA 2.5 (representative, NOT the Nothing Ear 3a, The Kit); the deep sky — File:ESO - Milky Way.jpg, CC BY 4.0, ESO (representative, Curiosities). The cover "declared vs built rings" hero, the World-Cup bracket, the Macro four-instrument strip/tables, the RAM-price bars, the sensor-comparison, the sideline-timeline, the cosmic-clock timeline and the essay's "two ways to end" figure kept as original SVG (no forced photo). THE LONG READ (3pp): **"The Sense of an Ending"** — the declared ending (a peace pronounced over; a market that un-priced it) vs the built ending (a rail loop finished on schedule after 17 yrs), via **Frank Kermode's *The Sense of an Ending* (1967)** ("tick-tock," "in the middest" — we impose endings reality doesn't offer), the **Compiègne (1918/1940) & Panmunjom (1953) armistices** (declarations mistaken for settlements; Fromkin's *A Peace to End All Peace*), **Fukuyama's 1989 "end of history"** (the ultimate *tock*), and the counter-image of **Amiens Cathedral** (patience organised into stone; the tree whose shade you'll never sit in, No. 36); the discipline = distrust endings that arrive as sentences, honour the ones that arrive as last pieces; "only the patient actually finish things"; Ecclesiastes anchor; callbacks to the harvest-lag (No. 36) & homecoming-as-practice (No. 35). Editorial theme: *an ending is built, not declared*.

Issue spine: *the calibrated blow — force used as correspondence; the message lives in what is withheld; watch what is spared, not what is struck*. Theme tag: *watch what is spared*. Clausewitz anchor; Ecclesiastes (No. 37) callback. Editorial theme: *watch what is spared*.

issues.quote: I refute it thus.
issues.author: Samuel Johnson, kicking a stone, as recorded in James Boswell's *Life of Johnson* (1791)
issues.note: **The Weekend Edition** (Saturday lifestyle-mode book, 28pp = the fixed twelve-desk 24pp book + the 4-page **Travel Desk** supplement; cover + 3 teasers led from The Good Life / Curiosities / The Grand Tour; hard-news desks lean & reflective). Issue spine: *the perceived and the real — some things are true whether or not anyone is watching; others are only true because enough people agreed*. THE WORLD (2pp, TWO viewpoint panels Washington/Gulf-GCC): LEAD "'over,' and still going" — Trump declared the Hormuz ceasefire framework "over" Fri 10 Jul while confirming Iran asked to keep talking and Doha negotiations (sanctions relief, frozen funds, the nuclear file) resume Sat 11 Jul; correction issued on No. 38's "Kharg spared" line — fresher reporting has assets on/near Kharg struck, tanker *Berg 1* still loading; Hormuz traffic slowed further; IEA global supply still 9.4m bpd below pre-war levels; fresh GCC statement sets independent terms (missiles/drones/proxies, guaranteed transit); World Cup QFs (Nor–Eng, Arg–Sui) + SK hynix's Nasdaq debut closed out (+13%, $168.01, largest-ever foreign US listing, beats Alibaba 2014 — CLOSED per New-Peg Test). SINGAPORE: LEAD — NE1 rehearsal show returns NDP to the National Stadium after a decade at the Padang (fireworks tonight); CAD/Police 2-week sweep (230 probed, 713 scam cases, ~S$9M losses) incl. a Singpass-harvesting job-offer ring; WP/Pritam Singh leadership question CLOSED (unopposed re-election, 28 Jun) — no new peg. PROPERTY: LEAD "one market, splitting in two" — URA Q2 flash +0.5% QoQ headline masks CCR +2.0% / landed +2.6% vs RCR −1.4% (first fall) / OCR −0.2% — a flight-to-prime rotation, not a cooling; Balestier Regency (4th en-bloc attempt) and High Point (5th) both closed with results still unreported. TECHNOLOGY (2pp): p7 Silicon & Sovereignty LEAD "the market just agreed with the hype" — SK hynix's Nasdaq debut resolved (belief priced, real trading, +13%); p8 The Home Lab — ComfyUI 0.27.0–0.27.1 (Seedream 5 Pro, Seed Audio 1.0, int8 quant) + native ROCm-on-Windows support in Comfy Desktop, closing the last AMD-vs-Nvidia software-convenience gap. THE KIT: LEAD "a cinema that folds into a case" — Xreal a01+ AR glasses first reviews ($299, 62g, 147" virtual screen, USB-C tethered) — the sub-$300 AR bracket is now a real category; Samsung Galaxy Glasses Unpacked (22 Jul) one-line. CONNECTED HOME: LEAD "Hue finally speaks Thread — almost on its own" — Hue firmware lets existing bulbs run Zigbee + Matter-over-Thread simultaneously; Bridge Pro remains a bridge, not a Border Router — a genuine but partial local-first upgrade. THE GOOD LIFE: OBJECT LEAD — First State Auctions' Australia's-largest-ever Swiss-watch consignment (28 lots, tomorrow) led by a Rolex Daytona "Rainbow" ref. 126598RBOW, first-ever example at auction anywhere, est. >$500k; Phillips H1 2026 watches = 46% of $507M total sales. SCREEN & SOUND: LEAD "reviews weren't lying, for once" — Moana's soft Thu previews ($4.5M) and sliding weekend tracking ($47–55M, was $70–89M) CLOSE the No. 38 sceptic's-test thread; Evil Dead Burn tracking $30–40M, a potential franchise record; Kelela's *new avatar* (Metacritic 88) the actual pick over the Stones' mixed *Foreign Tongues*. THE FAMILY DESK (2pp): LEAD — the People-First Chatbot Act (H.R. 9619, introduced 9 Jul) + RAND/*JAMA Pediatrics* (AI-chatbot mental-health use 12–21yo, 13.1%→19.2% in a year) with a "don't be alarmist" page distinguishing companion/romantic bots (the real risk category) from general-purpose homework helpers — usage skews 18–21, well outside an 11-year-old's band. THE MACRO DESK (four instruments): "a correction, on ourselves" — No. 38's Friday-morning JGB relief (2.77%) is contradicted by fresher reporting near a fresh 30-year high (~2.82%) — held as an unresolved conflict, not picked; world equities (proxied via S&P 500) extended to 7,575.39 on the SK hynix tailwind + discounted war premium (two engines, not one); STI record ~5,465; BTC through the $64k wall; gold rangebound $4,100–4,135; USD/SGD and MAS's July statement both held as stale/pending rather than invented. CURIOSITIES: LEAD "the shark nobody had seen alive" — goblin shark (*Mitsukurina owstoni*) filmed alive for the first time, two sightings (2019 Jarvis Is. 1,237m; 2024 Tonga Trench 1,997m, a new depth record), *Journal of Fish Biology*; secondary = ancient human DNA recovered from cave-wall rock art for the first time (*Nat. Commun.*, Spain/Portugal). LOVE & LIFE: LEAD "you don't need a twin, you need a fan" — a 1,484-person/371-quad friendship study finds PERCEIVED (not actual) similarity/favourable-trait-rating predicts satisfaction; paired with a 10-yr Danish divorce-conflict health-cost study. FITNESS: LEAD "lift heavy through the change" — STOP-EM (Univ. Calgary, *Bone Reports*, n=40): heavy (80–90% 1RM) supervised training preserved lean mass/leg power/bone density through perimenopause while the waitlist control group actively LOST ground — decline is the default, not a neutral holding pattern; Verdin/Kaeberlein biological-age-test scepticism as the recurring "boring beats flashy" sceptic box. THE TRAVEL DESK (4pp, weekend supplement): Departures — SIA returns to Madrid via Barcelona (26 Oct, first in 22 yrs, 15th European city), Scoot Vienna/Cairns frequency ups, Pontianak joins the Indonesia build-out, Japan's tripled (¥1,000→¥3,000) departure tax now IN FORCE (1 Jul); THE GRAND TOUR: Hokkaido (Niseko + the east) — chosen from the Destination Ledger for Furano/Biei's lavender peak bloom (10–25 Jul, this issue lands inside it), the Niseko-summer/Whistler-winter parallel, and eastern Hokkaido's dark skies as a secondary astro thread; honesty flags: SIA's own SIN–Sapporo service is winter-seasonal only (no July direct — check Scoot/ANA/JAL), Shirogane Blue Pond actually peaks before this window, Furano's summer tour buses run one departure/day with no add-ons. THE DIARY (2pp): SG — NE1 tonight, LEGO Botanicals @ Jewel, NDP 9 Aug; Japan — Mitama Festival (NEW), Gion Matsuri, Sumida Fireworks, Hiroshi Sugimoto/Ron Mueck exhibitions; region — Sydney Marathon (now a World Marathon Major, ★) & Hamilton Island Race Week. THE TABLE: FreakyNoods, Madeleine's Original Egg Tarts (nostalgia return, Aperia), Cafe ON:DO, Yunma Bakehouse — three of four honestly flagged "too new to call." PHOTO EDITION heroes (2, verified/representative): Marina Bay dusk (Singapore), wafer chips (Technology) — no new Commons verification possible this session (image-host fetch blocked in-sandbox); Hokkaido and other new subjects correctly kept as original SVG artwork rather than an unverified photo. THE LONG READ (3pp): **"I Refute It Thus"** — Berkeley's *esse est percipi* (1710) vs Samuel Johnson's kicked-stone rebuttal (Boswell, 1791) as the frame for telling which of the week's claims are true independent of observation (the shark, the lavender bloom, a bone's decline) and which are only true because enough people believe them (SK hynix's price, a friendship's perceived quality) — via Keynes's beauty-contest passage (*General Theory*, 1936, ch.12) for the second category, with the Hormuz ceasefire and the JGB-yield conflict as the hard middle case where the magazine had to model the discipline itself rather than just describe it; callbacks to No. 09 (the map is not the territory), No. 13 (the said and the done), No. 23 (the word that finally arrived). Editorial theme: *the stone and the contest*.

issues.quote: For one human being to love another: that is perhaps the most difficult of all our tasks... the work for which all other work is but preparation.
issues.author: Rainer Maria Rilke, *Letters to a Young Poet* (1929)
issues.note: **The Weekend Edition** (Sunday lifestyle-mode book, 28pp = the fixed twelve-desk 24pp book + the 4-page **Travel Desk** supplement; cover + 3 teasers led from The Good Life / Curiosities / The Grand Tour). Issue spine: *the long rehearsal — preparation that quietly turns out to already be the real thing (a spacecraft's practice flyby, a parade rehearsal, a resolution written for a crisis still unresolved), set against announcements that skip the rehearsal and claim to already be finished (Washington's "ceasefire over")*. THE WORLD (delta only from No. 39): LEAD "a label, and the room behind it" — Trump's "ceasefire over" declaration vs the Doha channel reconvening exactly where it left off, unresolved not restarted; the IMO adopted a Singapore-led, 30-co-sponsor resolution reaffirming free Hormuz transit rights (a rules-based marker, not a reopened strait — see Singapore). World Cup QF: Norway beat England 2–1 (Schjelderup, Bellingham, Torbjørn Heggem's winner) to reach the semis against the Argentina–Switzerland winner (14–15 Jul); Arg–Swi honestly reported unresolved at Singapore Sunday-morning press time rather than guessed. SINGAPORE: LEAD "thirty signatures, no applause" — the IMO resolution itself as the story (Singapore + 29 co-sponsors incl. Indonesia \& Malaysia); NDP's NE1 rehearsal ran on schedule at the National Stadium; El Niño/positive-IOD haze-risk advisory flagged, hot 33–34°C. PROPERTY: LEAD "two tenders, still not real" — Balestier Regency's 4th en-bloc attempt (tender closed 9 Jul) and High Point's 5th (closed 9 Jun) both remain genuinely unreported a month-plus on; a closed tender is not a completed sale; H2 2026 GLS pipeline (~61,000 units) noted as background scale, not a story. TECHNOLOGY: p7 Silicon \& Sovereignty LEAD "arriving before it was due" — Nvidia's Rubin architecture confirmed in full production roughly two quarters ahead of its original schedule, against a Blackwell backlog of ~3.6M units; p8 The Home Lab — Ollama closed a $65M Series B (Theory Ventures), 8.9M monthly active developers, framed against hyperscaler capex as "the other kind of AI money." THE KIT: Google \& Samsung's "Intelligent Eyewear" (Gemini-powered, Gentle Monster/Warby Parker design partners) — first public look, fall 2026 launch, audio-first + display tiers, ~$600–900 estimated; supersedes the stale No. 17 Android XR note. THE CONNECTED HOME: Home Assistant Green's retail price has doubled since its 2023 launch ($99→$199, Nabu Casa attributes it to RAM/component cost pass-through) — local-first holding to its principle, at a real and rising cost. THE GOOD LIFE: Sullivans Cove named World's Best Single Cask Single Malt for a 4th time (2026 World Whiskies Awards, no other distillery has matched it) — the whisky-trail credential behind this issue's Tasmania Grand Tour; the Rolex Rainbow Daytona sale (First State Auctions, No. 39) remains open, no hammer price yet. SCREEN \& SOUND: Evil Dead Burn's actual opening (\$14.5M domestic, \$6.5M first day) landed well under the \$25–35M franchise-record projections flagged last issue — tracking-vs-actual as the real story. THE FAMILY DESK (2pp): a large ABCD-study (Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development) analysis found parental limit-setting \& active monitoring predict lower problematic adolescent screen use, while a parent's OWN screen use predicts more of it — "look at your own phone," not a stricter stopwatch; "don't be alarmist" contrarian note included. THE MACRO DESK: markets closed since Friday for this Sunday-dated book — held not fabricated (S\&P{eq} 7,575.39, STI 5,469.29 +0.65% Fri, JGB 10Y still unresolved 2.77–2.82%, Brent \$71.2 cooling not cracking, Gold \$4,128.90, BTC ~\$64,340). CURIOSITIES: Hayabusa2's practice flyby of asteroid 98943 Torifune (800m closest approach, 5 Jul) — a deliberate rehearsal for the 2031 near-Earth-asteroid rendezvous, not a discovery in itself. LOVE \& LIFE: a new romantic-deception typology study (4 Jul, *Journal of Social and Personal Relationships*) sorting lies by underlying motive — "protecting the relationship" vs "protecting myself from it" — paired with a compatibility-perception study. FITNESS: a 143,715-adult, ~19.2-year-mean-follow-up JAMA Network Open study (Nurses' Health Study / Health Professionals Follow-Up) found SUSTAINED (not merely started) resistance training tied to a 27% (with ≥2 h/wk) to 42% (combined with aerobic activity) lower type 2 diabetes risk. THE TRAVEL DESK: Departures — Scoot's new thrice-weekly Chiang Rai route, SIA Hangzhou (daily) \& Riyadh (4x weekly) additions, RTS Link/ETIAS/Bali-levy held as continuity, no fresh peg; THE GRAND TOUR = **Tasmania, Australia** — Solar Maximum's peak aurora-australis window (2025–26), MONA, Salamanca Market, the Sullivans Cove whisky trail; an honest MONA family-content caveat and the ~11h25 no-direct-flight routing via Melbourne. THE DIARY: "The Table" led by MENSHO X's global-debut Raffles Place ramen outlet and Yi Man Fen Dessert's first-outside-China opening at 313 Somerset (both genuine international firsts, "too new to call" on the eating); Japan festival season (Mitama, Gion, Tenjin, Sumida fireworks) advanced delta-only. THE LONG READ: "The Long Rehearsal" — Rilke on love as the work all other work prepares for, threading Hayabusa2's flyby, the IMO resolution, NDP's rehearsal shows and Sullivans Cove's four wins as genuine (if incomplete) rehearsals, against Washington's "ceasefire over" and the two stalled en-bloc tenders as rehearsals with no guaranteed graduation.

issues.quote: The Moving Finger writes; and, having writ, / Moves on: nor all thy Piety nor Wit / Shall lure it back to cancel half a Line, / Nor all thy Tears wash out a Word of it.
